listenings.text: Every big conference has the same curve. On day one, your energy is high, but your listening is slow, because your ear is still adjusting. By the afternoon of day two, your listening finally warms up, but now the problem is different. It's cognitive load. Your brain is simply full. So here are my three rules for day two. First, protect your morning. Put the important meetings before lunch, not after. Second, don't fake it. If you lose the thread, say so early, with a clear phrase, like, could you hit the key point again? Nobody thinks you're weak. They think you're careful. And third, use the pause. Take two seconds before you answer a hard question. Silence feels long to you, but to the other person, it sounds like thinking.

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for staying with us. A few quick changes before we start. The regulatory panel was scheduled for four o'clock, but it's moving to four thirty, in Room 3B, because the keynote is running late. The speaker from the European Banking Authority had to cancel this morning, so her colleague is taking her place. If you were planning to attend the workshop on ISO 20022 testing, please note that it's now full, but the slides will be in the conference app tonight. And one last thing. The networking reception starts at six, not seven, so you have a little more time to rest between sessions.
